endorsements.quote: Uncertainty quantification is a promising approach to communicate AI confidence in recommendations to end users.
Our design concepts and alternative designs should be empirically tested and validated with target users to understand their impact on clinician-AI collaboration and appropriate reliance.
Continuing education programs and targeted trainings may serve as critical venues to broaden the AI capability and competency of the healthcare workforce.

Up-to-date information on algorithmic fairness and temporal trends from algorithmovigilance or AI monitoring systems may allow users to understand variations in their experience with model predictions, creating more trust in the AI system as a whole through transparency around model limitations.

Algorithmovigilance systems could be extended to monitor evolving trust and reliance by tracking temporal changes in correlations between patient outcomes, risk predictions, model performance, and indicators of user interactions with AI tools, as well as monitoring user feedback.
Model fact sheets or nutrition-style labels have been proposed by multiple organizations.

With this approach, clinicians can focus their critical appraisals on AI predictions flagged as less reliable, minimizing the cognitive burden and time needed to calibrate trust in a particular AI-DST prediction.

unlisted_practices: Disclose local model performance alongside AI predictions rather than encouraging users to trust that deployed models perform well locally.
Highlight temporal stability, recent performance deterioration, and model updates to users at the point of care.
Present subpopulation-specific performance information for the current patient at the point of care.
Visually flag each AI prediction with a checkpoint indicating whether performance, fairness, or uncertainty issues warrant further scrutiny, including for low-risk predictions.
Use human-centered design with end users to develop contextual AI explanations adapted to model type, use case, workflow, and user needs.
Localize models on local data and run shadow-mode prospective evaluations before go-live to establish baseline local performance.
Invest in algorithmovigilance systems and link their performance and fairness data to user-facing decision support.
Support low-resource health systems with minimum viable designs, common data models for temporal AI performance, open-source visualizations, vendor support, and collaborative networks.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper advocating for an expanded view of explainable AI incorporating contextual information across multiple levels to calibrate trust and reliance in clinical workflows.
